title: A record day at the New York City Marathon!
lead: On 1 November 2026, more than 60,000 runners finished the New York City Marathon. It was a new world record!
body: On Sunday 1 November 2026, a lot of people ran the New York City Marathon in the USA. A marathon is a very long race: 26.2 miles, or about 42 kilometres. The runners started on Staten Island, ran through the 5 boroughs (parts) of the city and finished in Central Park.
The winner of the men's race was Andreas Almgren from Sweden. He is 31 and it was his first marathon! He finished in 2 hours, 6 minutes and 1 second.
In the women's race, Sheila Chepkirui from Kenya won for the second time. An American runner, Jessica McClain, was second, only 6 seconds behind her.
In the wheelchair race, Marcel Hug from Switzerland won by just 1 second! And there was a world record: more than 60,000 runners finished the race. It was the biggest marathon in history!

title: No phones at school in England!
lead: The government says schools in England should be phone-free. How do the schools do it?
body: In England, the government wants all schools to be "phone-free". Pupils shouldn't use their mobile phones during lessons, between lessons, at break or at lunch.
Each school chooses how to do it. Some schools collect the phones in the morning. Others ask pupils to put them in a locker, or in a pouch: a small bag that stays closed until the end of the day.
In West Norfolk, in the east of England, some secondary schools already had a phone-free policy. Pupils can bring their phone to school, but they can't use it before they leave.
Why? The idea is to have fewer distractions in class, to help pupils concentrate, and to encourage them to talk to each other.

title: Are honey bees the bullies of the garden?
lead: Scientists in England watched bees for two years. They discovered that honey bees often push other insects away from flowers.
body: Researchers from Anglia Ruskin University watched pollinators – insects that carry pollen from flower to flower – in five places around Cambridge, in England. All the places were near a honey bee hive.

In total, they observed the insects for 93 hours. Honey bees started most of the fights and won most of them. Sometimes they pushed or chased other insects away. Bumblebees, wild bees and hoverflies often flew away when a honey bee arrived.
Where there were twice as many honey bees, there were 14% fewer bumblebees on the flowers. The competition was stronger when it was hot, so global warming could help honey bees even more.
The scientists don't say: "Stop keeping bees!" But there are more and more beekeepers in the UK: 19,000 in 2010 and 47,000 today. We need to protect wild pollinators too.

title: A new record on Mars!
lead: NASA's Perseverance rover is now the vehicle that has driven the farthest on another world.
body: Perseverance is a robot car, called a rover. It is on Mars, in a place called Jezero Crater. It arrived there in 2021.
On 11 October 2026, Perseverance broke a record. It has now travelled 45.22 kilometres on Mars. No other vehicle has driven so far on another planet or on the Moon!
The old record belonged to another NASA rover, Opportunity. It drove 45.16 kilometres on Mars and stopped working in 2018. Perseverance did it in about half the time.
How does it drive? Perseverance can think while it drives. It looks at the pictures from its cameras and chooses a safe way around the rocks. It can travel up to 412 metres in one Martian day.
